paper_metadata.title: Mechanical Properties of Multicomponent Titanium Alloy

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: A β-titanium alloy, obtained by cooling a melt at a rate of ~ 800°C/s, has been studied

evidence.section: Experimental Procedure
evidence.quote: A charge of mass 100 g was melted under purified argon by the electric are method with a nonconsumable tungsten electrode on a water-cooled copper hearth in an indentation of hemispherical geometry.

evidence.section: Experimental Procedure
evidence.quote: The small ingots obtained were remelted six or seven times to homogenize the composition

process_steps.method: rapid solidification (melt casting into water-cooled copper mold)

evidence.section: Experimental Procedure
evidence.quote: they were poured into a water-cooled copper mold 10 mm in diameter and 100 mm in length. Under these conditions, the cooling rate of the liquid melt in the copper mold is 800–900 °C.
subsequent annealing for 1 h at T =°750 C

evidence.quote: When the annealing temperature is raised to 1000°C, the two last phases containing Ga and Zr disappear.

attributes.size: dendrite colonies 10-20 um; dendrite globules 1-5 um; conglomerates 100-150 um
attributes.morphology: fine dendritic crystals with globular dendrite colonies

evidence.section: Phase Composition and Structural State of the Alloy
evidence.quote: The structure of the alloy has the appearance of fine dendritic crystals, which are relatively uniformly distributed in the ultrafine-grained matrix

attributes.morphology: interdendritic space with fine particles of minor phases

evidence.quote: Level 4 interdendritic space, which is a β-titanium based solid solution containing fine particles of minor phases.

evidence.section: Thermal Stability of the Alloy
evidence.quote: The TK35 cast alloy in the hardened state possesses high hardness values ( HIT = 9.5–10.5 GPa)

evidence.section: Thermal Stability of the Alloy
evidence.quote: Young’s modulus of the alloy E = 110–130 GPa.

evidence.section: Thermal Stability of the Alloy
evidence.quote: the noncontact elastic strain of the alloy (“purely” elastic strain which occurs in the alloy indentation region that is not in contact with the indenter) [10, 11] is at the level ε es = 25.%
